config.title: Context Performance

intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app with a counter and a theme toggle to explore how React Context can impact performance. You'll learn about the concept of unnecessary re-renders when context values change, and how to optimize them using techniques like memoization. The main technologies involved are React Context, the useState hook, and the React.memo higher-order component. By the end, you'll understand how to structure context providers and consumers to keep your app fast and efficient.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications like e-commerce sites or financial dashboards, React Context is often used to manage global state such as user preferences, theme settings, or shopping cart data. However, when a context value changes, it can cause unnecessary re-renders in many components, leading to performance issues in complex UIs with interactive filters, real-time data panels, or large product listings. Developers optimize context performance by splitting contexts, using memoization, or selective subscriptions to ensure that only the relevant parts of the UI update, maintaining a smooth user experience in high-traffic applications.

objectives: Construct a React Context provider with TypeScript interfaces for type-safe state management
Implement memoization techniques to prevent unnecessary re-renders in Context consumers
Configure Context value splitting to isolate performance-critical state updates
Apply the useMemo hook to optimize expensive computations within Context providers
Initialize custom Context hooks with proper TypeScript typing for consumer components
Integrate React.memo with Context consumption to control component re-renders
Manipulate Context provider hierarchies to minimize propagation of unnecessary updates
